old_caption:
The video showcases a large, intricate arrangement of colorful dominoes on a wooden floor. The dominoes are meticulously placed to form a detailed image of a yellow smiley face with red spots, set against a blue background. The smiley face is composed of numerous small dominoes, creating a pixelated effect. Surrounding the central image, there is a border made up of dominoes in various colors, forming a decorative frame.

As the video progresses, the dominoes begin to fall in a chain reaction, starting from the left side of the frame and moving towards the right. The dominoes in the border also start to topple, creating a wave-like effect that spreads across the entire arrangement. The falling dominoes create a dynamic and visually engaging sequence, with each piece crashing into the next, causing a cascading effect that gradually erases the initial image. The video captures the mesmerizing process of the dominoes toppling, highlighting the precision and art

caption:
The video showcases a large floor mosaic constructed from thousands of upright dominoes arranged as pixel art on a light wooden surface. The design depicts a yellow wedge of cheese dotted with red holes, set within a blue square field and ringed by a standing multicolored border, while a separate wavy line of flat dominoes lies outside the bordered square along the bottom edge. The camera remains fixed on the fully upright and undisturbed scene.

A collapse starts at the bottom-left corner of the blue field, where standing dominoes tip over into a flat dark patch. The fallen area expands along the bottom edge toward the center and climbs the left edge, progressively flattening the blue tiles as the front advances. The lower-left pointed tip of the yellow cheese falls, merging into the flattened region. The lower segment of the left multicolored border also topples, while the upper and right portions of the image remain standing.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
